A company has hired a solutions architect to design a reliable architecture for its application. The application consists of one Amazon RDS DB
instance and two manually provisioned Amazon EC2 instances that run web servers. The EC2 instances are located in a single Availability Zone.
An employee recently deleted the DB instance, and the application was unavailable for 24 hours as a result. The company is concerned with the
overall reliability of its environment.
What should the solutions architect do to maximize reliability of the application's infrastructure?
correctAnswer: Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection. Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer, and run them in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.
incorrectAnswers: Delete one EC2 instance and enable termination protection on the other EC2 instance. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.

Create an additional DB instance along with an Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. Configure the application to invoke the Lambda function through API Gateway. Have the Lambda function write the data to the two DB instances.

Place the EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group that has multiple subnets located in multiple Availability Zones. Use Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the health of the instances. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.
explanation:
Deletion protection prevents accidental DB deletion, Multi-AZ gives database failover, and an ALB with a multi-AZ Auto Scaling group removes the web tier single point of failure. Spot Instances reduce reliability.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-benefits.html

factChecks.explanation: Key deletes an EC2 instance (reducing reliability) and leaves web tier in one AZ. The correct choice is Multi-AZ RDS with deletion protection plus ALB and Auto Scaling across AZs.

question:
A company stores data in PDF format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must follow a legal requirement to retain all new and existing data in
Amazon S3 for 7 years.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Use S3 Batch Operations to bring the existing data into compliance.
incorrectAnswers: Turn on the S3 Versioning feature for the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Lifecycle to delete the data after 7 years. Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for all S3 objects.
Turn on S3 Object Lock with governance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
explanation:
Compliance mode prevents any user, including root, from deleting objects during retention. A default bucket retention applies only to new objects; S3 Batch Operations can set Object Lock retention on existing objects at scale.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops-retention-date.html

factChecks.explanation: Key is wrong. Versioning + lifecycle delete + MFA delete does not enforce retention. Accepted answer: Object Lock compliance mode with S3 Batch Operations to apply retention to existing objects (no recopy).

question:
A company has two VPCs named Management and Production. The Management VPC uses VPNs through a customer gateway to connect to a
single device in the data center. The Production VPC uses a virtual private gateway with two attached AWS Direct Connect connections. The
Management and Production VPCs both use a single VPC peering connection to allow communication between the applications.
What should a solutions architect do to mitigate any single point of failure in this architecture?
correctAnswer: Add a second set of VPNs to the Management VPC from a second customer gateway device.
incorrectAnswers: Add a set of VPNs between the Management and Production VPCs.
Add a second virtual private gateway and attach it to the Management VPC.
Add a second VPC peering connection between the Management VPC and the Production VPC.
explanation:
The single on-premises device on the Management VPC's VPN is the failure point; a second customer gateway device with its own VPN connection removes it. A peering connection is already redundant by design and the Production VPC has two Direct Connect connections.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-redundant-connection.html

factChecks.explanation: The Management VPC's single customer gateway device is the single point of failure; docs recommend a second VPN connection with a second customer gateway device.

question:
A company runs a Java-based job on an Amazon EC2 instance. The job runs every hour and takes 10 seconds to run. The job runs on a scheduled
interval and consumes 1 GB of memory. The CPU utilization of the instance is low except for short surges during which the job uses the maximum
CPU available. The company wants to optimize the costs to run the job.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Copy the code into an AWS Lambda function that has 1 GB of memory. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to run the code each hour.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Run the job as an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task on AWS Fargate with 0.5 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 1 GB of memory.
Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Install the container in the existing Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Ensure that the schedule stops the container when the task finishes.
Configure the existing schedule to stop the EC2 instance at the completion of the job and restart the EC2 instance when the next job starts.
explanation:
Lambda runs code without managing servers and bills only for the roughly 10 seconds per hour that it runs, triggered by an EventBridge schedule. Containerizing with App2Container onto Fargate or EC2 adds effort and cost for such a short job.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html

factChecks.explanation: A 10-second hourly job is the classic Lambda use case (pay per use, EventBridge schedule). Keyed Fargate option is more complex and costlier. Lambda handles 1 GB memory and is well under the 15-minute limit.

question:
A company wants to implement a backup strategy for Amazon EC2 data and multiple Amazon S3 buckets. Because of regulatory requirements,
the company must retain backup files for a specific time period. The company must not alter the files for the duration of the retention period.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in compliance mode. Create the required backup plan.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in governance mode. Create the required backup plan.
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create the required automated snapshot policy.
Use Amazon S3 File Gateway to create the backup. Configure the appropriate S3 Lifecycle management.
explanation:
AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode cannot be changed or deleted by anyone once the grace time expires, enforcing retention for EC2 and S3 backups. Governance mode can be removed by users with sufficient permissions.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/vault-lock.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed governance mode is wrong for 'must not alter'. Users with sufficient IAM permissions can remove a governance-mode vault lock. Compliance mode is immutable after the grace time, which meets regulatory WORM requirements.

question:
A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to back up the EC2 instances to a second
Region. The company also wants to provision EC2 resources in the second Region and manage the EC2 instances centrally from one AWS
account.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup. Configure cross-Region backup to the second Region for the EC2 instances.
incorrectAnswers: Create a disaster recovery (DR) plan that has a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Configure data replication.
Create point-in-time Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the EC2 instances. Copy the snapshots to the second Region periodically.
Deploy a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data from the source Region to the second Region.
explanation:
AWS Backup centrally schedules EC2 backups and copies them across Regions without running duplicate instances. Running a similar fleet in the second Region (DR plan or DataSync) is far more costly.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/cross-region-backup.html

factChecks.explanation: AWS Backup with cross-Region copy gives centralized management and backup to a second Region most cost-effectively; a standing duplicate fleet and replication is costly. EBS snapshot copy is defensible but lacks central management.

question:
A company that uses AWS is building an application to transfer data to a product manufacturer. The company has its own identity provider (IdP).
The company wants the IdP to authenticate application users while the users use the application to transfer data. The company must use
Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) protocol.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Transfer Family to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
Use Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task for IdP authentication.
Use AWS Storage Gateway to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool for IdP authentication.
explanation:
AWS Transfer Family supports the AS2 protocol and can use a Lambda function to integrate a custom identity provider. DataSync, AppFlow and Storage Gateway do not provide AS2.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html

factChecks.explanation: AS2 is supported by AWS Transfer Family, which supports custom identity providers via Lambda. DataSync does not support AS2.

question:
A company wants to securely exchange data between its software as a service (SaaS) application Salesforce account and Amazon S3. The
company must encrypt the data at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys (CMKs). The company must
also encrypt the data in transit. The company has enabled API access for the Salesforce account.
correctAnswer: Create Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
incorrectAnswers: Create AWS Lambda functions to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Define the task to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
Create a custom connector for Salesforce to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
explanation:
Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed service to securely exchange data between SaaS apps such as Salesforce and Amazon S3, encrypting data in transit and at rest (with customer managed KMS keys). Lambda or Step Functions require custom code to build and maintain.

question:
A company is developing a mobile gaming app in a single AWS Region. The app runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.
The company stores the app data in Amazon DynamoDB. The app communicates by using TCP traffic and UDP traffic between the users and the
servers. The application will be used globally. The company wants to ensure the lowest possible latency for all users.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB.

Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB. Update CloudFront to use the NLB as the origin.

Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB. Update CloudFront to use the ALB as the origin.
explanation:
NLB supports TCP and UDP listeners and is a Global Accelerator endpoint; ALB listeners support only HTTP and HTTPS; CloudFront does not proxy arbitrary UDP.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-listeners.html

factChecks.explanation: Key is wrong. ALB listeners support only HTTP/HTTPS, not UDP. Global Accelerator with an NLB (TCP/UDP) is correct.

question:
A company has an application that processes customer orders. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that saves the
orders to an Amazon Aurora database. Occasionally when traffic is high the workload does not process orders fast enough.
What should a solutions architect do to write the orders reliably to the database as quickly as possible?
correctAnswer: Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.
incorrectAnswers: Increase the instance size of the EC2 instance when traffic is high. Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic.

Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SNS topic.

Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when the EC2 instance reaches CPU threshold limits. Use scheduled scaling of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.
explanation:
SQS durably buffers orders so none are lost, and an Auto Scaling group of consumers drains the queue as fast as demand requires. SNS is push-based and cannot deliver to a database endpoint, and queuing only at a CPU threshold with scheduled scaling does not respond to unpredictable traffic.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer subscribes a database endpoint to SNS, which is not possible (SNS cannot write to an Aurora endpoint) and does not buffer. Decoupling with an SQS queue and an Auto Scaling consumer fleet writes orders reliably and scales with load.

question:
An IoT company is releasing a mattress that has sensors to collect data about a user’s sleep. The sensors will send data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
The sensors collect approximately 2 MB of data every night for each mattress. The company must process and summarize the data for each
mattress. The results need to be available as soon as possible. Data processing will require 1 GB of memory and will finish within 30 seconds.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Lambda with a Python script
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS Glue with a Scala job
Use Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark script
Use AWS Glue with a PySpark job
explanation:
Lambda can be invoked by S3 event notifications as each file arrives, supports up to 10,240 MB of memory and 15-minute runs, and bills per millisecond, so a 30-second, 1 GB job is cheapest and fastest on Lambda. Glue and EMR are built for large distributed jobs and have minimum billing and startup overhead.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-memory.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed Glue Scala job is wrong. A per-object job needing 1 GB memory and finishing in 30 seconds fits AWS Lambda (up to 10,240 MB, 15 min) triggered by S3, billed per ms. Glue and EMR have higher minimum billing and startup latency.

question:

Nitro-based instances within the same Availability Zone. The company also wants to give the application the ability to write to multiple block
storage volumes in multiple EC2 Nitro-based instances simultaneously to achieve higher application availability.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
incorrectAnswers: Use General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach

explanation:

question:

member account, the account no longer receives the full benefit of the Compute Savings Plan commitment. The company uses less than 50% of
its purchased compute power.
correctAnswer: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the company's Organizations management account.
incorrectAnswers: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the member account that purchased the Compute Savings Plan.

factChecks.explanation: Stem is missing its question sentence. Discount sharing is controlled from the management account of the organization, not the member account; Savings Plans cannot be sold on the RI Marketplace.

question:
A company is developing a microservices application that will provide a search catalog for customers. The company must use REST APIs to
present the frontend of the application to users. The REST APIs must access the backend services that the company hosts in containers in private
VPC subnets.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
incorrectAnswers: Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
explanation:
The requirement is REST APIs, and API Gateway reaches private VPC resources through a VPC link private integration. A WebSocket API does not meet the REST requirement, and a security group alone cannot connect API Gateway to private subnets.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-private-integration.html

factChecks.explanation: Question requires REST APIs; keyed answer uses a WebSocket API. REST API with a VPC link to private ECS is correct (security groups cannot be used for API Gateway access).

question:
A company stores raw collected data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is used for several types of analytics on behalf of the company's
customers. The type of analytics requested determines the access pattern on the S3 objects.
The company cannot predict or control the access pattern. The company wants to reduce its S3 costs.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
incorrectAnswers: Use S3 replication to transition infrequently accessed objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
Use S3 Inventory to identify and transition objects that have not been accessed from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
explanation:
S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the recommended class for data with unknown or unpredictable access patterns and moves objects between tiers automatically with no retrieval fees. Standard-IA adds retrieval charges and replication does not transition storage classes.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering.html

factChecks.explanation: Unpredictable access pattern -> S3 Intelligent-Tiering (lifecycle transition). Key (replication to Standard-IA) is wrong: replication copies objects, does not transition, and Standard-IA charges retrieval fees for unpredictable access. Explanation is about S3 Express One Zone.

question:
A company has applications hosted on Amazon EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses. The applications must initiate communications with other
external applications using the internet. However the company’s security policy states that any external service cannot initiate a connection to the
EC2 instances.
What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?
correctAnswer: Create an egress-only internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
incorrectAnswers: Create a NAT gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
Create an internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
Create a virtual private gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
explanation:
An egress-only internet gateway allows outbound IPv6 traffic and blocks connections initiated from the internet. NAT gateways serve IPv4 and an internet gateway would allow inbound connections.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/egress-only-internet-gateway.html

factChecks.explanation: For IPv6 outbound-only, use an egress-only internet gateway; NAT gateway (the key) is for IPv4.

question:

the development phase, the application will store and access 1 TB of data in Amazon S3 each day. The company wants to minimize costs and
wants to prevent traffic from traversing the internet whenever possible.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC
incorrectAnswers: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the S3 bucket
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the S3 bucket
Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC
explanation:
A gateway endpoint lets VPC resources reach S3 over the AWS network without an internet gateway or NAT, at no additional charge. Interface endpoints for S3 incur hourly and data processing charges, and Intelligent-Tiering or Transfer Acceleration do not keep traffic off the internet.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer (Intelligent-Tiering) does not address keeping traffic off the internet or minimizing transfer cost. A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 is free and keeps traffic on the AWS network; interface endpoint costs extra.

question:
A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a
recent application launch requirement, the company’s VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
incorrectAnswers: Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications.
explanation:
Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub and supports inter-Region peering attachments, avoiding the n-squared peering connections. VPC peering is non-transitive and requires many connections; Direct Connect gateways and PrivateLink are not intended for general VPC-to-VPC routing.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-peering.html

factChecks.explanation: Full-mesh VPC peering across many VPCs/Regions is high administrative effort and non-transitive. Transit Gateway per Region plus inter-Region TGW peering is the least-effort hub-and-spoke solution.

A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new
users on AWS. The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on
department.
Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?
correctAnswer: Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permission. Attach the policy to the IAM groups
incorrectAnswers: Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions
Create IAM roles that have least privilege permission. Attach the roles to the IAM groups
Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions
explanation:
IAM best practice is to apply least-privilege policies and attach them to groups so new users inherit them. SCPs and permissions boundaries only limit permissions and grant none, and roles are not attached to groups.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html

factChecks.explanation: SCPs never grant permissions, and IAM roles cannot be attached to groups. Attaching a least-privilege policy to the groups is the answer. Ligatures dropped.

Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Implement the write-through caching strategy
incorrectAnswers: Implement the lazy loading caching strategy
Implement the adding TTL caching strategy
Implement the AWS AppConfig caching strategy
explanation:
Write-through updates the cache whenever data is written to the database, so cached data is never stale. Lazy loading only populates on a cache miss and TTL only bounds staleness.

factChecks.explanation: Key (lazy loading) does not update the cache on writes and can serve stale data; write-through adds or updates the cache whenever data is written to the database, so it always matches.

data storage. The application traffic will be unpredictable. The company expects that the application read and write throughput to the database
will be moderate to high. The company needs to scale in response to application traffic.
Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.
incorrectAnswers: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.
explanation:
On-demand mode scales automatically for unpredictable traffic with pay-per-request pricing and no capacity planning. Standard-IA is for rarely accessed data (higher request cost), and provisioned with auto scaling needs forecasting.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/capacity-mode.html

factChecks.explanation: Unpredictable traffic with scaling need points to on-demand capacity, which is the recommended default; provisioned requires forecasting. Standard-IA class suits infrequently accessed data, not moderate-to-high throughput.

question:
A solutions architect is reviewing the resilience of an application. The solutions architect notices that a database administrator recently failed
over the application's Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database writer instance as part of a scaling exercise. The failover resulted in 3 minutes of
downtime for the application.
Which solution will reduce the downtime for scaling exercises with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.
incorrectAnswers: Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.
Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.
explanation:
RDS Proxy makes applications resilient to database failover by connecting to the standby/new writer while preserving application connections, cutting perceived downtime. Replicas, a second cluster, or a cache add complexity and do not speed the failover.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.html

factChecks.explanation: Adding read replicas does not shorten the failover itself for a scaling exercise; RDS Proxy preserves application connections and routes to the new writer, reducing failover downtime with minimal change (endpoint swap).

The company wants to expand globally and to ensure that its application has minimal downtime.
Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?
correctAnswer: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.
incorrectAnswers: Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
explanation:
An Auto Scaling group spans Availability Zones within one Region only, so a second Region needs its own deployment. Aurora Global Database replicates with typically sub-second lag and supports promoting a secondary Region, and Route 53 failover routing shifts traffic when health checks fail.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html

A data analytics company wants to migrate its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically
during the day through FTP. An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job takes hours to finish running.
The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the
files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully. Processing for each le needs to take 3-8
minutes.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.
incorrectAnswers: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.

Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
explanation:
Transfer Family provides a managed FTP endpoint backed by S3 so clients barely change, and S3 events trigger Lambda immediately for each file. Transfer Family stores to S3 or EFS, not EBS, and nightly or Glacier processing misses the requirement.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer processes nightly from Glacier (violates 'as soon as possible') and runs self-managed FTP on EC2. Transfer Family (FTP) to S3 + S3 event + Lambda (3-8 minutes fits 15-minute limit) is the most operationally efficient.

centralized account. The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket in the centralized account to store the VPC flow logs and AWS CloudTrail
logs. All logs must be highly available for 30 days for frequent analysis, retained for an additional 60 days for backup purposes, and deleted 90
days after creation.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Transition objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
incorrectAnswers: Transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.

explanation:
Objects start in S3 Standard for the 30 days of frequent analysis, then move to low-cost Glacier Flexible Retrieval as backup until expiring at day 90. Transitioning to Standard does nothing, and moving to Glacier at day 90 is meaningless because the objects are deleted then.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer transitions to S3 Standard 30 days after creation (objects already start in Standard) so there is no backup tier. Intended answer: transition to Glacier Flexible Retrieval at 30 days and expire at 90. Other options move to Glacier at 90 days, the same day objects expire. Note Glacier has a 90-day minimum duration charge.
